findings.reason: the stated mechanism (directories resolved at plan build and read from the plan) cannot satisfy the section's own second case on a resume or a lane change, both of which rebuild from the recorded row; the deliverable must name carrying the lane's declared search path onto the rebuilt backend, as the placement and gate-document carries already do.
findings.text: §21's second case asserts that "a resume of that run composes a supervisor spec whose PATH contains it too", but on the resume path the backend mapping is rebuilt by `_backend_settings` (reckon/crew/dispatch_sessions.py:911), which returns a fresh `{launch, command}` dict plus only five copied keys (`dialect`, `usable_input_window`, `model`, `effort`, `input_modalities`) when the record names a command, so the project-declared `search_path` is absent; the resume then adds back only single keys through `_carry_declared_placement` (:1026) and `_carry_declared_gate_documents` (:1051), so the plan built from that mapping carries no directories and the resumed supervisor spec's PATH omits the declared directory

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — every named symbol resolves at base: `LaunchPlan` (reckon/_backends.py:394), `resolve_launch_executable` (reckon/crew/dispatch_launch.py:1184), `_persisted_worker_environment` (:730), `_supervisor_spec` (:2411), the availability report's `shutil.which` (reckon/flight.py:2349); commit d8d93ea4 exists, is absent from main's history and is pinned at refs/reckon/archive/a-launch-finds-its-backend-on-the-declared-path, which is what makes "read it with `git show`" correct; 5631154f78 is an ancestor of HEAD and is §20's recorded run head, whose declared-path input landed in code at 600cba4d68. Two "near line" hints lag their symbols (dispatch.py:3164 → 3233; dispatch_launch.py:670 → 730) but resolve through the symbol named beside each, so they mislead no reader who follows the name.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §21's second case (a resume whose supervisor-spec PATH carries the project-declared directory) is not produced by the mechanism §21 states, because the backend mapping a resume rebuilds from drops `search_path` (FINDING reasoning below); §22's case and its negative control hold, since a bare `shutil.which` leaves the off-PATH stub unfound.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — both gates write their logs under the run directory (`~/.config/reckon/crew/runs/<run_id>/`), a durable path that outlives the node, and both name their new test file repo-relative; nothing is directed at a scratchpad or a node-local temporary directory.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the new test filenames are behavioural (`test_every_backend_reader_searches_the_declared_path.py`, `test_the_availability_report_searches_the_declared_path.py`), and neither section carries a plan label, stage name, ticket number or changelog sentence.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §21's root cause matches its evidence (reckon/crew/dispatch.py:3233 and reckon/crew/dispatch_sessions.py:1849 pass no `backend` to `resolve_launch_executable`, and `_declared_search_path_for_backend_name` reads `flight.resolve()` with no project), but its mechanism does not produce the resume arm it asserts; §22's mechanism does run on a real path, `probe_availability` (reckon/flight.py:2306), which two production callers reach (reckon/flight.py:2720, reckon/crew_dispatch_commands.py:619) with project-resolved backend entries.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §21 carries one deliverable (a project-layer search path reaches every reader of a cli launch) and §22 one (the availability report searches the declared path); splitting the report out of §21 is what keeps each on one verdict.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — §21's declared depends-on §20 is present in plan-section-depends-on (plan.html:29), and §22 consumes only §20's already-landed `search_path` key (reckon/_flight_schema.py:355), which is an ancestor of HEAD at 600cba4d68, so §22 carries no undeclared wait that the queue would need to hold; no declared relationship points at a node that does not exist.
